e-8273.knowledge_point: Calculating a Vector Given Its Coordinates Relative to a Basis
e-8273.problem:
Consider the polynomials $p_1(t)$ and $p_2(t),$ given by

$$
p_1(t)=3+2t, \qquad
	p_2(t)=-t+t^2.
$$

Find $p(t)$ given that $\mathcal{B}=\big\{ p_1(t), p_2(t) \big\}$ is a basis of $\textrm{Span}\big\{ p_1, p_2 \big\},$ and the coordinates of $p(t)$ relative to $\mathcal{B}$ are ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068026/assets/3274a690fa59f7d7368fcbe54004eab244c9845e20bf03ffce1e9fa25bbaf4bc.png)
e-8273.worked_solution:
Any vector in $\textrm{Span}\big\{ p_1, p_2 \big\}$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068026/assets/170acd827e8b97471869159c5d9af88b0e4324b25ca1b42ec652011ece6a5174.png)

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}p(t) & =4\cdot (3+2t)+(-3)\cdot (-t+{t}^{2}) \\  & =12+8t+3t-3{t}^{2} \\  & =12+11t-3{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

e-8274.knowledge_point: Finding the Coordinates of a Vector With Respect to a Given Basis in a Matrix Vector Space
e-8274.problem:
Consider the following matrices:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068026/assets/8a495251bb5d61eab1568624a6e1c213ccee49ec98fc8d5ff5c17fc841d027bf.png)
If $\mathcal B = \{B_1,B_2\}$ is a basis of $\textrm{Span}\{ B_1, B_2 \},$ calculate ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068026/assets/342997674c65cf5c4d14f0b2a7df2649bf99a8b0c003be93efa983f317faa7a1.png)
e-8274.worked_solution:
We need to find $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that 

$$
x_1 B_1 +x_2 B_2 = A.
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 8 & -4\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} & 0 \\ 8{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2} & -4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-5 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding entries, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=-5 \\ 8{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=-2 \\ -4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068026/assets/ebd814bcb627ef3b9208bc0960bdaf48b9448396ed7e95d18d8c4abbf1169244.png)

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & -5 \\ 8 & -2 & -2 \\ -4 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-4){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & -5 \\ 0 & 2 & 18 \\ 0 & -1 & -9\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=-5 \\ 2{x}_{2}=18 \\ -{x}_{2}=-9.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second and third equations, we get $x_2 =9.$ From the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-9 & =-5 \\ 2{x}_{1} & =4 \\ {x}_{1} & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068026/assets/dfc845ca1739c329e5636726466c76efee7eba19df4adc0909110506f894e72d.png)

e-8275.knowledge_point: Finding the Coordinates of a Vector With Respect to a Given Basis in a Polynomial Vector Space
e-8275.problem:
Consider the following polynomials:

$$
p_1(t)=5+t^2, \quad
p_2(t)=3t-2t^2, \quad
q(t)=5-3t+3t^2.
$$

If $\mathcal{B}=\{ p_1(t), p_2(t) \}$ is a basis of $\textrm{Span}\big\{ p_1(t), p_2(t) \big\},$ find $[q(t)]_{\mathcal{B}}.$
e-8275.worked_solution:
We need to find $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that 

$$
x_1 p_1(t)+x_2 p_2(t) = q(t)
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(5+{t}^{2})+{x}_{2}(3t-2{t}^{2}) & =5-3t+3{t}^{2} \\ 5{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}t+({x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}){t}^{2} & =5-3t+3{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}=5 \\ 3{x}_{2}=-3 \\ {x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=3.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068026/assets/195a50f130cc40c4a725066035f2da3ef25b725df96601e53f70716bd82b4f4a.png)

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 \\ 1 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-\frac{1}{5}){R}_{1} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 \\ 0 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+\frac{2}{3}{R}_{2} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 3 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}5{x}_{1}=5 \\ 3{x}_{2}=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

From the first and second equations, we get $x_1=1$ and $x_2 =-1.$ Therefore, ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14068026/assets/9f23f71e833d7a7f81f511e1dfb72861ed753cb514de43d6cabfeb3c6b65fadb.png)

after.problem:
Consider the polynomials ${p}_{1}(t)$ and ${p}_{2}(t),$ given by

$$
{p}_{1}(t)=2t+{t}^{3},\,{p}_{2}(t)=3-t-3{t}^{3}.
$$

Find $p(t)$ given that $B={{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}{{p}_{1},{p}_{2}},$ and the coordinates of $p(t)$ relative to $B$ are $[p(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
Any vector in  $\text{Span}{{p}_{1},{p}_{2}}$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
[p(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}p(t) & =2\cdot (2t+{t}^{3})+2\cdot (3-t-3{t}^{3}) \\  & =4t+2{t}^{3}+6-2t-6{t}^{3} \\  & =6+2t-4{t}^{3}.\end{aligned}

a
p(t)=3+2t+4t3
b

c
p(t)=6−2t+4t3
d
p(t)=6+2t−4t3
e
p(t)=3+t−2t3
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Any vector in Span{p1,p2} can be written as

x1p1(t)+x2p2(t).

In our case, we have

[p(t)]B=[x1x2]=[22].

Therefore,

p(t)=2⋅(2t+t3)+2⋅(3−t−3t3)=4t+2t3+6−2t−6t3=6+2t−4t3.

content.knowledge_point: Calculating a Vector Given Its Coordinates Relative to a Basis
content.problem:
Consider the polynomials ${p}_{1}(t)$ and ${p}_{2}(t),$ given by

$$
{p}_{1}(t)=2t+{t}^{3},\,{p}_{2}(t)=3-t-3{t}^{3}.
$$

Find $p(t)$ given that $B={{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}{{p}_{1},{p}_{2}},$ and the coordinates of $p(t)$ relative to $B$ are $[p(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
Any vector in  $\text{Span}{{p}_{1},{p}_{2}}$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
[p(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}p(t) & =2\cdot (2t+{t}^{3})+2\cdot (3-t-3{t}^{3}) \\  & =4t+2{t}^{3}+6-2t-6{t}^{3} \\  & =6+2t-4{t}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem:
Consider the polynomials ${p}_{1}(t)$ and ${p}_{2}(t),$ given by

$$
{p}_{1}(t)=1+t+{t}^{2},\,{p}_{2}(t)=1+t-{t}^{2}.
$$

Find $p(t)$ given that $B={{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}{{p}_{1},{p}_{2}},$ and the coordinates of $p(t)$ relative to $B$ are $[p(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
Any vector in  $\text{Span}{{p}_{1},{p}_{2}}$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
[p(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}p(t) & =(-1)\cdot (1+t+{t}^{2})+1\cdot (1+t-{t}^{2}) \\  & =-1-t-{t}^{2}+1+t-{t}^{2} \\  & =-2{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the polynomials p1(t) and p2(t), given by p1(t)=1+t+t2,p2(t)=1+t−t2. Find p(t) given that B={p1(t),p2(t)} is a basis of Span{p1,p2}, and the coordinates of p(t) relative to B are [p(t)]B=[−11].

a
2+2t
b
−2t2
c
t2
d
0

Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Any vector in Span{p1,p2} can be written as

x1p1(t)+x2p2(t).

In our case, we have

[p(t)]B=[x1x2]=[−11].

Therefore,

p(t)=(−1)⋅(1+t+t2)+1⋅(1+t−t2)=−1−t−t2+1+t−t2=−2t2.

content.knowledge_point: Calculating a Vector Given Its Coordinates Relative to a Basis
content.problem:
Consider the polynomials ${p}_{1}(t)$ and ${p}_{2}(t),$ given by

$$
{p}_{1}(t)=1+t+{t}^{2},\,{p}_{2}(t)=1+t-{t}^{2}.
$$

Find $p(t)$ given that $B={{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}{{p}_{1},{p}_{2}},$ and the coordinates of $p(t)$ relative to $B$ are $[p(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
Any vector in  $\text{Span}{{p}_{1},{p}_{2}}$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
[p(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}p(t) & =(-1)\cdot (1+t+{t}^{2})+1\cdot (1+t-{t}^{2}) \\  & =-1-t-{t}^{2}+1+t-{t}^{2} \\  & =-2{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Consider the polynomials ${p}_{1}(t)$ and ${p}_{2}(t),$ given by

$$
{p}_{1}(t)=2{t}^{2}+{t}^{3},\,{p}_{2}(t)=1+3{t}^{2}.
$$

Find $p(t)$ given that $B={{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}{{p}_{1},{p}_{2}},$ and the coordinates of $p(t)$ relative to $B$ are $[p(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
Any vector in  $\text{Span}{{p}_{1},{p}_{2}}$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
[p(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}p(t) & =3\cdot (2{t}^{2}+{t}^{3})+(-2)\cdot (1+3{t}^{2}) \\  & =6{t}^{2}+3{t}^{3}-2-6{t}^{2} \\  & =-2+3{t}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Consider the polynomials ${p}_{1}(t)$ and ${p}_{2}(t),$ given by

$$
{p}_{1}(t)=1-t+2{t}^{2},\,{p}_{2}(t)=t-{t}^{2}.
$$

Find $p(t)$ given that $B={{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}{{p}_{1},{p}_{2}},$ and the coordinates of $p(t)$ relative to $B$ are $[p(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
Any vector in  $\text{Span}{{p}_{1},{p}_{2}}$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
[p(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}p(t) & =1\cdot (1-t+2{t}^{2})+3\cdot (t-{t}^{2}) \\  & =1-t+2{t}^{2}+3t-3{t}^{2} \\  & =1+2t-{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

a

b
p(t)=1+2t−6t2
c
p(t)=1−3t−t2
d
p(t)=1+2t−5t2
e
p(t)=1+4t−t2

Correct
EXPLANATION

Any vector in Span{p1,p2} can be written as

x1p1(t)+x2p2(t).

In our case, we have

[p(t)]B=[x1x2]=[13].

Therefore,

p(t)=1⋅(1−t+2t2)+3⋅(t−t2)=1−t+2t2+3t−3t2=1+2t−t2.

Consider the polynomials ${p}_{1}(t)$ and ${p}_{2}(t),$ given by

$$
{p}_{1}(t)=1-t+2{t}^{2},\,{p}_{2}(t)=t-{t}^{2}.
$$

Find $p(t)$ given that $B={{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}{{p}_{1},{p}_{2}},$ and the coordinates of $p(t)$ relative to $B$ are $[p(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
Any vector in  $\text{Span}{{p}_{1},{p}_{2}}$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
[p(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}p(t) & =1\cdot (1-t+2{t}^{2})+3\cdot (t-{t}^{2}) \\  & =1-t+2{t}^{2}+3t-3{t}^{2} \\  & =1+2t-{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
$$
{A}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}],\,{A}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above. Find the matrix $C$ given that $B={{A}_{1},{A}_{2}}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}{{A}_{1},{A}_{2}},$ and the coordinates of the matrix $C$ relative to $B$ are $[C]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
Any vector in $\text{Span}{{A}_{1},{A}_{2}}$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{A}_{1}+{x}_{2}{A}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
[C]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =(-2)\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]+2\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 2 & -4\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 4 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 6 & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Calculating a Vector Given Its Coordinates Relative to a Basis
content.problem:
$$
{A}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}],\,{A}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above. Find the matrix $C$ given that $B={{A}_{1},{A}_{2}}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}{{A}_{1},{A}_{2}},$ and the coordinates of the matrix $C$ relative to $B$ are $[C]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
Any vector in $\text{Span}{{A}_{1},{A}_{2}}$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{A}_{1}+{x}_{2}{A}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
[C]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =(-2)\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]+2\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 2 & -4\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 4 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 6 & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
{B}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}],\,{B}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}6 & 3 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 \\ -4 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

If $B={{B}_{1},{B}_{2}}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}{{B}_{1},{B}_{2}},$ and $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],$ then ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=$
after.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{B}_{1}+{x}_{2}{B}_{2}=A.
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}6 & 3 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 \\ -4 & 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2} & -{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} & 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 \\ -4 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding entries, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}=-2 \\ -{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=5 \\ 3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=-4.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}4 & 6 & -2 \\ -1 & 3 & 5 \\ 3 & 2 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}4 & 6 & -2 \\ -1 & 3 & 5 \\ 3 & 2 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{4}{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-\frac{3}{4}){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}4 & 6 & -2 \\ 0 & \frac{9}{2} & \frac{9}{2} \\ 0 & -\frac{5}{2} & -\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}=-2 \\ \frac{9}{2}{x}_{2}=\frac{9}{2} \\ -\frac{5}{2}{x}_{2}=-\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second and third equations, we get ${x}_{2}=1.$ From the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+6\cdot 1 & =-2 \\ 4{x}_{1} & =-8 \\ {x}_{1} & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-2+1=-1.$

content.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{B}_{1}+{x}_{2}{B}_{2}=A.
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}6 & 3 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 \\ -4 & 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2} & -{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} & 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 \\ -4 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
{B}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,{B}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ -4 & 0\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

If $B={{B}_{1},{B}_{2}}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}{{B}_{1},{B}_{2}},$ and $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],$ then ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=$
after.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{B}_{1}+{x}_{2}{B}_{2}=A.
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ -4 & 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} & -3{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{1}-4{x}_{2} & 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding entries, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=1 \\ -3{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ -3 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & -4 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ -3 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & -4 & -1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 9 & 3 \\ 0 & -6 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=1 \\ 9{x}_{2}=3 \\ -6{x}_{2}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second and third equations, we get ${x}_{2}=\frac{1}{3}.$ From the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2\cdot \frac{1}{3} & =1 \\ {x}_{1} & =1-\frac{2}{3} \\ {x}_{1} & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{3}=\frac{2}{3}.$

$$
{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}=2 \\ 5{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=1 \\ 4{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=3.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 2 \\ 5 & -3 & 1 \\ 4 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 2 \\ 5 & -3 & 1 \\ 4 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-\frac{5}{4}){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & -\frac{3}{2} \\ 0 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2}=1.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 20 & -2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0 & 2{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} & -2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 20 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding entries, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=4 \\ 3{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=20 \\ -2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 4 \\ 3 & 4 & 20 \\ -2 & 3 & -2\end{aligned}].

$$

$$

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=4 \\ 7{x}_{2}=14 \\ {x}_{2}=2.\end{aligned}

$$

content.problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
{B}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}],\,{B}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 20 & -2\end{aligned}]
$$

If $B={{B}_{1},{B}_{2}}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}{{B}_{1},{B}_{2}},$ and $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],$ then ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=$
content.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{B}_{1}+{x}_{2}{B}_{2}=A.
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 20 & -2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0 & 2{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} & -2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 20 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding entries, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=4 \\ 3{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=20 \\ -2{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 4 \\ 3 & 4 & 20 \\ -2 & 3 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 4 \\ 3 & 4 & 20 \\ -2 & 3 & -2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-\frac{3}{2}){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 7 & 14 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=4 \\ 7{x}_{2}=14 \\ {x}_{2}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second and third equations, we get ${x}_{2}=2.$ From the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-2\cdot 2 & =4 \\ 2{x}_{1} & =8 \\ {x}_{1} & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=4+2=6.$

$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

We need to find ${x}_{1},{x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t)+{x}_{3}{p}_{3}(t)=q(t).
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}({t}^{2}+t)+{x}_{2}({t}^{2}-2t+4)+{x}_{3}({t}^{3}-2{t}^{2}-2) & =2+{t}^{2}+{t}^{3} \\ (4{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3})+({x}_{1}-2{x}_{2})t+({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}){t}^{2}+{x}_{3}{t}^{3} & =2+{t}^{2}+{t}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain 

$$
{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=2 \\ {x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=1 \\ {x}_{3}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 & -2 & 2 \\ 1 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}0 & 4 & -2 & 2 \\ 1 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & {R}_{1}↔{R}_{2} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & -2 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-\frac{3}{4}){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -\frac{1}{2} & -\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+2{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -\frac{1}{2} & -\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0 \\ 4{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=2 \\ -\frac{1}{2}{x}_{3}=-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=1.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
4{x}_{2}-2\cdot 1=2\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=1.
$$

Now, substituting the obtained value into the first equation, we get

$$
{x}_{1}-2\cdot 1=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=2.
$$

Therefore, $[q(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ and therefore ${x}_{1}=2.$

content.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1},{x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t)+{x}_{3}{p}_{3}(t)=q(t).
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}({t}^{2}+t)+{x}_{2}({t}^{2}-2t+4)+{x}_{3}({t}^{3}-2{t}^{2}-2) & =2+{t}^{2}+{t}^{3} \\ (4{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3})+({x}_{1}-2{x}_{2})t+({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}){t}^{2}+{x}_{3}{t}^{3} & =2+{t}^{2}+{t}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain 

$$
{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=2 \\ {x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=1 \\ {x}_{3}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 & -2 & 2 \\ 1 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}0 & 4 & -2 & 2 \\ 1 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & {R}_{1}↔{R}_{2} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & -2 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-\frac{3}{4}){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -\frac{1}{2} & -\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+2{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -\frac{1}{2} & -\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0 \\ 4{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=2 \\ -\frac{1}{2}{x}_{3}=-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=1.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
4{x}_{2}-2\cdot 1=2\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=1.
$$

Now, substituting the obtained value into the first equation, we get

$$
{x}_{1}-2\cdot 1=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=2.
$$

Therefore, $[q(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ and therefore ${x}_{1}=2.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(2{t}^{2}+t-2)+{x}_{2}({t}^{2}+3t-6)+{x}_{3}(-2{t}^{3}+3{t}^{2}) & =-2{t}^{3}+4{t}^{2}+3t-6 \\ -2{x}_{3}{t}^{3}+(2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}){t}^{2}+({x}_{1}+3{x}_{2})t+(-2{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}) & =-2{t}^{3}+4{t}^{2}+3t-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{3}=-2 \\ 2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=4 \\ {x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=3 \\ -2{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}=-6.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 2 & 1 & 3 & 4 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 & 3 \\ -2 & -6 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 2 & 1 & 3 & 4 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 & 3 \\ -2 & -6 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & {R}_{1}↔{R}_{3} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -2 \\ -2 & -6 & 0 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & -5 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=3 \\ -5{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=-2 \\ -2{x}_{3}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get ${x}_{3}=1.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
-5{x}_{2}+3\cdot 1=-2\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=1.
$$

Now, substituting the obtained values into the first equation, we get

$$
{x}_{1}+3\cdot 1=3\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=0.
$$
